Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

## Diagnosis
The current bug report mentions miscellaneous issues in the "optimization" package, specifically mentioning changes related to [MATH-394](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-394), [MATH-397](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-397), and [MATH-404](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-404). One of the issues highlighted is related to the "BrentOptimizer" class which is part of the optimization package.

Looking at the failing test `testQuinticMin` in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizerTest`, it instantiates a `BrentOptimizer` with certain parameters and then uses it within a `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` instance. The test aims to optimize a quintic function and asserts the expected optimum value.

Recent bug reports indicate past issues with the `BrentOptimizer`, specifically mentioning a "buggy implementation" of Brent's optimization algorithm in the class "BrentOptimizer" within the optimization.univariate package.

## Steps to Reproduce the Bug
1. The test instantiates a `BrentOptimizer` with certain parameters.
2. It then uses this `BrentOptimizer` within a `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`.
3. The optimization process may not be functioning correctly due to potential issues in the `BrentOptimizer` class, as reported in recent bug reports.

The changes introduced in revisions related to [MATH-394](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-394), [MATH-397](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-397), and [MATH-404](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-404) may have affected the `BrentOptimizer` implementation causing the test to fail.

This suggests that the bug may be due to issues with the `BrentOptimizer` implementation within the "optimization.univariate" package.

## Potential Fix
- `BrentOptimizer.optimize` method may require inspection and potential fixes related to optimization algorithm implementation.

Next, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this bug.
